subject: Nonexclusive output pathways — MSA & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@archontech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ArchonTech Legal <legal@archontech.com>, Connor Blaine <connor@archontech.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MSA/Order Form redlines — output ownership & training

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency profile and how Redwood could fit into our customer-facing product. Our legal team has a few material concerns in the redlines attached to the MSA and Order Form (see attached Archon_Redlines_MSA.docx). The highlights: 

- Output ownership: We need clarity that outputs generated by the model when ArchonTech data is provided are owned by ArchonTech or, minimally, ArchonTech receives a perpetual, nonexclusive right to use and sublicense those outputs.
- Training/data use: ArchonTech cannot consent to any training of models on customer inputs unless we opt in via a separate agreement. We want an explicit opt-out-by-default for training and model retention of customer data.
- Feedback license: For any aggregated feedback or telemetry you ingest from ArchonTech, we want it limited to product safety/bugfix purposes and not used to train commercial models unless separately licensed.

Can Redwood propose language that preserves your ability to improve service quality while protecting our customer's IP and PII? If so, please send a mark or proposed clause. Procurement is keen to move quickly if we can close these points.

Attachments: Archon_Redlines_MSA.docx (redlines)

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Ops, ArchonTech
Alicia.gomez@archontech.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@archontech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form redlines — output ownership & training

Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Appreciate the urgency.

High level response: we can absolutely accept the principle of customers retaining ownership of outputs produced from their inputs, and we can draft a narrow service-level nonexclusive license to allow Redwood to use outputs for debugging, safety, and service improvements only. For training on long-term model weights, we agree to opt-in only (customer must explicitly enable).

Proposed next steps:
- I'm attaching a short proposed clause (redwood_proposed_clause.txt) that attempts to balance both sides: limited nonexclusive rights for Redwood for internal safety/improvement purposes, explicit opt-out for training, and a restricted feedback license for aggregated/anonymous telemetry.
- I'll loop in Karthik (product/legal liaison) and Laura (legal) to get faster alignment on the exact phrasing.
- If that looks OK to ArchonTech in principle, we can exchange a clean redline and push the Order Form to procurement for signature.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether ArchonTech needs output attribution (i.e., a requirement that downstream uses of model outputs carry a notice) or if a simple ownership/rights clause is sufficient? That will determine the final language.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwoodinference.com

Subject: FW: MSA/Order Form redlines — output ownership & training

Team — forwarding ArchonTech's redlines (attached) and my quick take. Procurement wants this wrapped this week if we can meet their constraints.

My suggested compromise (see attached redwood_proposed_clause.txt):
1) Output ownership: "ArchonTech owns Outputs (defined as content generated by the Service in response to Customer Inputs). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, nonexclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, distribute, and create Derivative Works of Outputs. Redwood may retain a copy of Outputs for the sole purpose of debugging, safety, and service performance improvements, provided such retention is limited in time and not used to train general-purpose model weights without Customer opt-in."

2) Training/data use: "Customer Data and Outputs are not used to update model weights or training datasets for production models unless Customer has provided prior written consent. Aggregated, de-identified telemetry may be used for internal analytics and to improve the technical performance of the Service, provided that no Customer PII or Confidential Information is included."

3) Feedback license: "To the extent Customer or its End Users provide Feedback (error reports, labels, prompts) to Redwood, Customer grants Redwood a limited, royalty-free, perpetual, worldwide license to use Feedback internally for service maintenance, safety, and operational improvements. Any use of Feedback to train or tune models that will be commercially distributed will require separate written agreement."

Questions for legal: is the term 'Derivative Works' acceptable here, or do we need different wording? Also propose a retention cap: 90 days for raw Outputs, 1 year for de-identified telemetry used for system metrics.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_clause.txt, link to internal Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-archon-msaredlines

—Priyom

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@archontech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor Blaine <connor@archontech.com>, ArchonTech Legal <legal@archontech.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form redlines — output ownership & training

Priyom, Karthik, Laura —

Thanks for the quick proposal and the suggested wording — overall this maps to what ArchonTech needs. A few small edits before we finalize: 

- Output retention: can we tighten raw Outputs retention to 30 days instead of 90? Our security team flagged longer windows as a risk.
- Feedback license: request explicit language that Feedback used for product improvement is limited to non-identifiable, aggregated telemetry and that any element intended for model training must be documented in a separate SOW.
- Attribution: ArchonTech does not require downstream attribution for general use, but we do insist on a notice if Outputs are redistributed to third parties as-is (i.e., a copy of output published unchanged should carry a short notice). Sample sentence included in the attached countersigned OrderForm_v3.pdf stub.

We also need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an export-control clause confirmation (Archon operates in regulated markets). Can you point us to the SOC2 report or an attestation URL?

If Redwood accepts the 30-day raw retention and the clarified feedback limitation, ArchonTech is prepared to sign the Order Form in the attached PDF and move to PO. Procurement expects the final MSA redline within 48 hours.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Ops, ArchonTech
